title: site-astro has two independent stylesheets that must be hand-kept in sync
incidentAliases: token fixed on one page only
summary: site-astro has three page-level stylesheets that redefine the same things independently, and what is shared versus duplicated has MOVED: the text ramp is now centralised, everything else still is not. landing.css (home) and docs.css (docs, blog, and the base how.css rides on) each still define --frost/--ember/--line/--void and the whole nav and footer layout independently, so a change to one leaves the other silently stale. But --text/--muted/--faint/--ink/--prose are now defined ONLY in styles/backdrop.css, which every page shell imports last. That move was forced by a real drift: body.essay-page had been repaired to a readable --prose with a comment reading 'was #8b9ab2 at 6.9:1', so the blog got fixed while docs and the landing page kept a grey that measured 4.30:1 - below the AA floor - once the background field changed what text sat on. The same class of drift is still live for the container width: .docs was 1200px/24px while .nav-in and .wrap are 1120px/28px, which put the docs content edge 44px left of the nav's until it was fixed this session. backdrop.css is the pattern to copy for anything that must not drift; how.css is the other good pattern - zero tokens of its own, riding docs.css.

home tokens and nav layout; no longer defines the text ramp, still owns --frost/--ember/--line and its own nav rules
docs+blog; redefines the same accent tokens and nav dimensions independently; .docs must stay 1120/28 to match .wrap
the good pattern - scoped overrides only, no tokens or nav rules of its own
imports landing.css then backdrop.css - the required order

invariants: The text ramp (--text/--muted/--faint/--ink/--prose) is defined ONLY in backdrop.css. Redefining any of them in a page stylesheet reintroduces the drift that made the blog readable and the docs not.
backdrop.css is also the ONLY place a page-wide background may be defined. A per-section background paints over the shared field and re-bands the page.
landing.css and docs.css intentionally share identical hex values for --frost/--ember/--line/--void - a palette change in one needs the matching edit in the other by hand.
Every content container is 1120px with 28px padding (.wrap, .nav-in, .docs). A container with its own width misaligns against the nav.
A shared component's chrome rules live in BOTH stylesheets, so deleting one (as with the .tl traffic-light dots) means deleting it twice.
